deep.reconstruction:
This page is a draft, with many deletions, of the introduction and table of contents for Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle's Journal 54, 1857). The next page is the covering letter to the journal's editor (Borchardt) sending that paper. The page contains no derivation in the strict sense. Its mathematical content is as follows.

(1) Plan. The paper has a first division of definitions and preliminary material, sections I–IV ('Definitionen', '... Ausdrücke', III, IV left blank). In the second division the Jacobi inversion problem is solved for an arbitrary system of everywhere-finite integrals (first-kind integrals) of 'gleichverzweigte' algebraic functions, that is, of one Riemann surface of genus p.

(2) The tool is the p-fold infinite theta series
 theta(v_1,...,v_p) = Sum_{m in Z^p} exp( Sum_{mu,mu'} a_{mu mu'} m_mu m_mu' + 2 Sum_mu m_mu v_mu ),
 with Riemann's normalisation (real part of the quadratic form negative definite). The exponent is illegible on the page; I take it from the published paper (§17).

(3) Moduli count. For the inversion problem only a special kind of these series is needed. Among the p(p+1)/2 quantities a_{mu mu'} there hold (p-2)(p-3)/2 relations, so only 3p-3 remain arbitrary. The bracketed qualifier probably means relations exist only for p>3.
- Arithmetic check (mine): p(p+1)/2 - (p-2)(p-3)/2 = (6p-6)/2 = 3p-3.
- This is the dimension count for the period matrices of genus-p curves inside the Siegel space. It is stated, essentially in these words, in the published 1857 introduction. Riemann derives 3p-3 there from the count of branch points / birational classes.

(4) Local uniformisation fragments, 'dx/dt dz^{1/tau - 1}', 'dz/dt ds^{1/tau-1}', and the remarks on chi, psi.
- At a branch point of order tau take z - a = t^tau. Then dt/dz ~ (z-a)^{1/tau - 1}.
- So a function that is finite and nonvanishing in the local parameter t behaves like dz^{1/tau-1} times a regular factor.
- The notes require auxiliary functions chi, psi to vanish like f(s) dz^{1/tau-1} where the surface winds around the point. Then the represented functions and their derivatives remain finite.
- The case of two 'sich aufhebende' (mutually cancelling) branch points that coincide is to be noted separately, referring to 'Art. 8'. At such a point the surface does not actually wind, and the condition differs. This matches the published Art. 7/8 discussion of coincident branch points.

(5) Literature. The inversion problem is Jacobi's, cited as 'd. J. Bd. 9 Abh. 32 §7' (Crelle 9, 1832, Considerationes generales de transcendentibus Abelianis). Weierstrass had published his solution in the hyperelliptic case 'in ihren Resultaten' (Crelle 47, 1854) together with a notation system for hyperelliptic functions. Riemann remarks on extending a notation to general Abelian functions and on avoiding double notation. This also matches the published introduction.
errors: No mathematical error on the page. The count p(p+1)/2 - (p-2)(p-3)/2 = 3p-3 is correct.

Edge case: the formula (p-2)(p-3)/2 would give 1 relation for p=1 and 3p-3 = 0 moduli. For p=1 there is in fact 1 modulus, so the statement tacitly assumes p>1 (indeed p>3 for nonzero relations). The bracket '(von p=3)' is most likely '(wenn p>3)'.
The theta exponent and the first displayed series are illegible and partly struck. The reconstruction of the exponent is taken from the published paper, not read from the page.

results.what: Jacobi inversion problem solved for arbitrary genus-p Riemann surface via p-fold theta series
results.modern_name: Riemann's solution of the Jacobi inversion problem; Riemann theta function

results.what: Riemann period matrices satisfy (p-2)(p-3)/2 relations among p(p+1)/2 entries, leaving 3p-3 free moduli
results.modern_name: dim M_g = 3g-3; codimension of the Jacobian locus (Schottky problem)

results.what: Local behaviour at branch points via the local parameter t with z-a=t^tau, factor dz^{1/tau-1}
results.modern_name: local uniformizing parameter at a ramification point

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of the published introduction to Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen (1857). The 3p-3 moduli count, the Weierstrass reference and the branch-point remarks all appear in print. Its interest is genetic, as a draft text alongside the covering letter, not mathematical novelty.

checkable.asserts: p(p+1)/2 minus (p-2)(p-3)/2 relations leaves 3p-3 free moduli
No relations for p=2,3; the first relation (Schottky) appears at p=4
With z-a=t^tau, dz = tau t^(tau-1) dt, so dt/dz is proportional to (z-a)^(1/tau-1)

transcription_corrections: 'D. J. Cod. 9. Abs. 32. S. 7.' should read 'd. J. Bd. 9. Abh. 32. §. 7.' (dieses Journals Band 9, Abhandlung 32, §7), i.e. Jacobi's 'Considerationes generales de transcendentibus Abelianis', Crelle 9 (1832).
'II. Rest[?] [?] Ausdrücke' is likely 'II. Hülfssätze / ... Ausdrücke'; uncertain.
'Art. 8' refers to an article of the published paper (discussion of coincident branch points).
